messages.lock.toast: Create or join a cloud first
messages.lock.canvasAria: Local star map: this device is not initialized
messages.lock.settings.title: Cloud not initialized
messages.lock.settings.desc: The main console is locked. Sharing, Memories, Audit, the device card, and data actions become available after you create or join a cloud. Setup completes in this process; no restart needed.
messages.lock.settings.foot: If you already initialized from the CLI but still see the locked console, restart the daemon so this process loads the new config.
messages.lock.settings.initializing: Setup is in progress. Try again in a moment.
messages.legend.title: Legend
messages.legend.note: Local view: only relationships with known peers, not the full network topology.
messages.status.degraded.p2pOff: P2P is off. Only local memories and subscriptions are shown; connections and sync are unavailable.
messages.banner.error: Can’t reach the local daemon: {message} (last data kept)
messages.onboard.coach.title: Create a cloud or join an existing one
messages.onboard.coach.bodyBefore: A cloud is the shared space for this device’s memories. Start from the top right:
messages.onboard.create.title: New cloud
messages.onboard.create.desc: Generates the root master key and initializes in this process. Sharing, Memories, Audit, and the device card unlock immediately; no restart needed.
messages.onboard.create.error.cloudName: Enter a cloud name (up to 24 characters).
messages.onboard.create.success: Cloud created. The console is unlocked.
messages.onboard.join.title: Join cloud
messages.onboard.join.lead: Paste the one-time token from the inviter’s Invite device panel. The master key isn’t copied; this console unlocks as soon as you join.
messages.onboard.join.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token text (or the text from the QR code)…
messages.onboard.join.error.token: Paste a join token first (the one-time token from the invite panel).
messages.onboard.join.success: Joined the cloud. The console is unlocked.
messages.onboard.error.invalidName: Names must be 1–24 characters and can’t contain /, \, or ..
messages.onboard.error.tokenInvalid: The token format is invalid. Ask the inviter to generate a new one.
messages.onboard.error.tokenExpired: The token expired. Ask the inviter to generate a new one.
messages.onboard.error.tokenRejected: The token is invalid or already used. Ask the inviter to generate a new one.
messages.onboard.error.endpointUnreachable: Can’t reach the inviter. Confirm their daemon is running and the address is reachable, then retry.
messages.onboard.error.notInitialized: Setup didn’t finish (no initialized flag). Retry, or check the daemon version.
messages.cloud.error.tokenInvalid: The token format is invalid. Ask the inviter to generate a new one.
messages.cloud.error.tokenExpired: The token expired. Ask the inviter to generate a new one.
messages.cloud.error.tokenRejected: The token is invalid or already used. Ask the inviter to generate a new one.
messages.cloud.error.invalidName: Cloud names must be 1–24 characters and can’t contain /, \, or ..
messages.cloud.error.nameTaken: A cloud with that name already exists. Choose another name.
messages.cloud.error.cloudArchived: Archived clouds can’t be renamed. Switch to it first.
messages.cloud.error.cloudBlocked: This device was removed from the current cloud and can’t rename it.
messages.cloud.error.profileNotFound: Cloud not found. The list may have changed; refresh and retry.
messages.cloud.error.profileJoinFailed: Couldn’t create the cloud. The token may already be redeemed; ask the inviter to generate a new one.
messages.cloud.error.endpointUnreachable: Can’t reach the inviter. Confirm their daemon is running and the address is reachable, then retry.
messages.cloud.error.cloudAlreadyJoined: This device already joined that cloud. You can switch to it.
messages.cloud.error.cloudDisabled: Cloud management isn’t available with a custom home or in this restricted environment. The current cloud is unchanged.
messages.cloud.error.cloudUnavailable: Cloud management isn’t available with a custom home or in this restricted environment. The current cloud is unchanged.
messages.cloud.error.cloudUnsupported: This daemon doesn’t support cloud management. Upgrade Mebular; the current cloud is unaffected.
messages.cloud.error.cloudListFailed: Couldn’t read the cloud list. The current cloud is unchanged; retry later.
messages.cloud.error.cloudRegistryInvalid: Cloud list unreadable (registry damaged). The current cloud is unchanged; repair the registry first.
messages.cloud.error.cloudRegistryLocked: Another process is writing the cloud list. Try again later.
messages.cloud.error.cloudProfilePathInvalid: Cloud directory is out of bounds; the operation was refused. The current cloud is unchanged.
messages.cloudJoin.title: Join cloud
messages.cloudJoin.lead: Paste the one-time token from the inviter. The master key isn’t copied.
messages.cloudJoin.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token text (or the text from the QR code)…
messages.cloudJoin.warning.switch: After joining, this console switches to the new cloud. The current cloud “{name}” is archived, not deleted.
messages.cloudJoin.warning.manual: After joining, follow the prompt to switch. The current cloud “{name}” is archived, not deleted.
messages.cloudJoin.inspect.meta: Inviter device {deviceId} · Shared domain {namespace} · Valid until {expires}
messages.cloudJoin.inspect.duplicate: This device already joined “{name}”. You can switch to it.
messages.cloudJoin.result.switching: Switching to the new cloud… The console refreshes automatically when the app finishes.
messages.cloudJoin.result.manual: You’re still on “{oldName}”. Run the command below to switch. The previous cloud is archived, not deleted.
messages.cloudSwitch.title: Switch to “{name}”
messages.cloudSwitch.progressNote: The current cloud “{name}” is archived, not deleted. The console refreshes automatically when done.
messages.cloudSwitch.submittedNote: The console refreshes automatically when the app finishes. If the old cloud still appears, retry shortly.
messages.cloudSwitch.submittedJoin: Switch submitted. The console refreshes automatically when the app finishes.
messages.cloudSwitch.fallbackNote: This page can’t switch clouds directly (not in the desktop app). The current cloud is still “{current}” and won’t change by itself.
messages.cloudSwitch.fallbackWarning: Run the command below in a terminal to switch to “{name}”. The previous cloud is archived, not deleted.
messages.cloudSwitch.manual: Copy the command and switch in a terminal. The current cloud is unchanged.
messages.cloudSwitch.confirm.title: Switch cloud
messages.cloudSwitch.confirm.body:
Switch to “{name}”?

The current cloud “{current}” is archived, not deleted; you can switch back anytime.
messages.cloudSwitch.confirm.label: Switch to “{name}”
messages.invite.title: Invite device
messages.invite.safety: One-time use · Share only in person or over a trusted LAN. Regenerating invalidates the old token; existing invites can no longer be redeemed.
messages.invite.lead: Scan to join, or copy the token.
messages.invite.token.label: One-time token
messages.invite.token.fingerprintTitle: Token fingerprint: changes when the token is regenerated
messages.invite.qrUnavailable: QR code unavailable. Copy the token instead.
messages.invite.ttl.label: Valid
messages.invite.regen.success: Token regenerated. The old token is now invalid.
messages.invite.regen.failed: Couldn’t regenerate: {message}. The previous token is still shown.
messages.invite.joinDisabled.note: Join service is off. Enable it to redeem a one-time token on a new device (the master key isn’t copied; tokens last 15 minutes by default).
messages.invite.joinDisabled.help: Writes joinService.enabled=true and restarts the daemon (service-managed restarts automatically; in the foreground, restart as prompted).
messages.invite.enablingNote: Enabling the join service and writing config… The daemon restarts, then token generation continues automatically.
messages.invite.enableFailed.title: Couldn’t write the join service config.
messages.invite.enableFailed.retryHelp: Try again. If it keeps failing, check config.json write permissions or the daemon log.
messages.invite.enableFailed.readonlyHelp: This console is read-only; memory.admin write access is required.
messages.invite.pending.note: After restart the daemon reads the new config. Click Retry to generate the token and QR code.
messages.invite.warning.loopback: Endpoint is loopback-only. Set joinService.bind to 0.0.0.0 and regenerate.
messages.invite.warning.invalid: Invalid endpoint address. Check the join service in Settings → Advanced.
messages.invite.warning.unreachable: Endpoint unreachable. Check the join service settings.
messages.wizard.aria: Connect a known device manually (transport repair)
messages.wizard.title: Connect a known device
messages.wizard.local.note: If a device already in this cloud stays offline, paste its address here to repair transport. This only fixes connectivity; trust and subscriptions don’t change.
messages.wizard.note.connected: Transport repaired. Return to the star map to see if the device is online. If not, check the port/firewall and retry.
messages.wizard.note.failed: Check that the peer runs serve, the multiaddr includes /p2p/<peerId>, and the port is reachable. Then retry.
messages.wizard.successToast: Connected. Return to the star map to check whether the device is online.
messages.settings.loading: Loading settings… (if this keeps happening, check that serve is running)
messages.settings.mock.commonNote: ?mock=1 only provides the security card and a read-only demo; editable settings need a live daemon.
messages.settings.mock.assistants: ?mock=1 has no demo data for AI assistants.
messages.settings.common.inviteDisabled: Disabled (enable it from “Invite device” in the top bar)
messages.settings.common.note: Editable settings live under Advanced and MCP; security actions live under Security.
messages.settings.pending.head: Configuration saved; this instance still runs the configuration it started with
messages.settings.pending.note: The daemon reads configuration only at startup; saved values take effect after a restart.
messages.settings.pending.noteEnv: Environment variables take precedence when set (current: {vars}).
messages.settings.pending.reasonFallback: Pending restart: saved values take effect after a restart
messages.settings.pending.manual: Not running as a service (foreground nohup): one-click restart is unavailable; restart manually with the command above.
messages.settings.apply.inProgress.note: The daemon is restarting (fields={fields}); once it is back this banner shows whether the change applied or rolled back.
messages.settings.apply.applied.note: Applied with the saved values ({time}); the pending-restart list is now empty.
messages.settings.apply.mismatch.summary: {count} fields differ from the saved values after the restart
messages.settings.apply.rolledBack: Rolled back to the last working configuration
messages.settings.editor.mismatch: ⚠ Mismatch: the written value is not in effect; the runtime value is authoritative
messages.settings.editor.notInSchema: (this field is not declared in the schema)
messages.settings.section.resident.title: Resident service
messages.settings.section.resident.desc: Enable this before inviting devices; the address and port decide whether a new device can connect.
messages.settings.section.network.title: Network
messages.settings.section.network.desc: Connectivity between this device and your cloud; when off, only this device works.
messages.settings.section.automation.title: Automation
messages.settings.section.automation.desc: Background maintenance and optional features; the defaults suit most people.
messages.settings.section.mcp.connection.title: Connection
messages.settings.section.mcp.connection.desc: Agents connect to this device over MCP; changes immediately affect console access.
messages.settings.section.mcp.tls.title: TLS
messages.settings.section.mcp.tls.desc: Encrypts MCP connections; required when listening beyond loopback.
messages.settings.mcp.danger.1: Changing auth, listen address or TLS can cut off the console immediately; you get one more confirmation before it is written.
messages.settings.mcp.danger.2: Locked out with bearer: paste a token from token grant to recover.
messages.settings.mcp.danger.3: Locked out with oauth or a port change: edit config.json back and restart mebular serve.
messages.settings.fields.mcpAuth.label: Auth
messages.settings.fields.mcpAuth.help: none for loopback only; bearer uses a token; oauth uses an environment secret.
messages.settings.fields.mcpHost.help: Defaults to 127.0.0.1; non-loopback requires auth and TLS.
messages.settings.fields.mcpTls.help: Missing certificates make startup fail; there is no silent downgrade.
messages.settings.fields.mcpTlsCert.label: Certificate path
messages.settings.fields.mcpTlsCert.help: PEM certificate; only applies together with the private key.
messages.settings.fields.mcpTlsKey.label: Private key path
messages.settings.fields.mcpTlsKey.help: PEM private key; only applies together with the certificate.
messages.settings.fields.joinEnabled.help: Issues one-time invite tokens; changes need a restart.
messages.settings.fields.joinBind.help: 0.0.0.0 allows LAN access; use only on trusted networks.
messages.settings.fields.joinPort.help: Default 4002; change it when the port is taken.
messages.settings.fields.networkEnabled.help: When off, this device works offline only.
messages.settings.fields.networkListen.help: Leave empty for the default; loopback only means the LAN cannot reach you.
messages.settings.fields.antiEntropy.label: Auto reconcile
messages.settings.fields.semantic.label: Enable semantic recall
messages.settings.fields.semantic.help: Needs a local model; falls back to keywords when it is missing.
messages.settings.service.title: Resident
messages.settings.service.note: Starts at login and restarts after a crash. Home {home} (see “About this device” for the service file path).
messages.settings.service.msg.restartRequested: Restart requested; this page recovers on its own shortly.
messages.settings.service.msg.installed: Now running as a resident service.
messages.settings.service.msg.uninstalled: No longer running as a resident service.
messages.settings.service.msg.failed: Could not finish: {message}. Try Recheck or copy the diagnostics.
messages.settings.wizard.title: Setup wizard
messages.settings.wizard.note: Walk through first-time setup again (existing configuration is kept)
messages.settings.cloud.title: Cloud
messages.settings.cloud.intro: Joining a cloud does not change the current one; the previous cloud is archived and can be switched back to at any time.
messages.settings.cloud.note: The current cloud cannot be switched to; switching to an archived cloud asks for confirmation. Renaming syncs to every device and needs no restart; archived clouds must be switched to before renaming.
messages.settings.cloud.duplicate: This device has a cloud with the same name: the current cloud shows a warning dot. Rename the one marked “Most recent · rename suggested”.
messages.settings.cloud.row.switchHint: Switch to this cloud to rename it
messages.settings.cloud.row.renameNote: Renaming syncs to every device (root fingerprint and trust stay the same).
messages.settings.diag.noApply: No “save and apply” record in this process yet.
messages.settings.diag.applyStatus.rolledBack: New configuration not in effect: rolled back
messages.settings.diag.raw.title: Full configuration
messages.settings.diag.lastApply.title: Last apply result
messages.settings.diag.connection.title: Manual connection
messages.settings.diag.connection.note: When a device in the same cloud stays disconnected, paste its multiaddr to establish transport; this does not change membership trust or subscriptions.
messages.settings.diag.recovery.title: Recovery guide
messages.settings.diag.recovery.authBody: bearer: paste a token from mebular token grant --scope memory.read,memory.admin to recover; oauth: a static token returns 401 invalid token and /register returns 404 by default (missing MEBULAR_OAUTH_ADMIN_SECRET / MEBULAR_OAUTH_REGISTER_SECRET) — edit config.json, set mcp.http.auth back to none (loopback only) and restart mebular serve.
messages.settings.diag.recovery.hostBody: Non-loopback requires auth≠none plus TLS and certificates, otherwise serve refuses to start; set it back to 127.0.0.1, or supply all three and restart.
messages.settings.diag.recovery.certBody: tls=true without tlsKey/tlsCert → startup fails with MCP_INSECURE_CONFIG (no silent downgrade): add the paths or turn TLS off.
messages.settings.diag.recovery.consoleBody: Check mebular status and the serve log: MCP_STORAGE_LOCKED means another instance holds the lock; MCP_INSECURE_CONFIG means the host/auth/tls combination is invalid.
messages.settings.security.loading: Loading security status… (shows — on an older daemon or a read failure; other settings are unaffected)
messages.settings.security.level.title: Security level
messages.settings.security.level.desc: The higher the tier, the higher the bar for sensitive actions.
messages.settings.security.totp.title: Authenticator seed
messages.settings.security.totp.desc: Medium-risk actions need a 6-digit code; the seed stays on this device only.
messages.settings.security.recovery.title: Recovery code
messages.settings.security.recovery.desc: The offline key for the High tier; shown only once, store it offline.
messages.settings.security.tier.low.title: Low (default)
messages.settings.security.tier.medium.title: Medium · authenticator code
messages.settings.security.tier.high.title: High · device co-sign
messages.settings.security.tier.high.note: Another device checks the pairing code to prevent forgery; applies to later actions only.
messages.settings.security.boundary: Medium stops a casual hand, not a stolen key: whoever takes the device takes the seed too. High needs another device present, or the offline recovery code when it is not.
messages.settings.security.totp.foot: The seed stays on this device; if every device is lost, root resets it — without a master key backup it cannot be recovered.
messages.settings.security.totp.mismatch: Import again from a device that holds the same seed; mismatched seeds are rejected.
messages.settings.security.recovery.notGenerated: Not generated (created when upgrading to High)
messages.settings.security.approval.verifyMeta: Compare digit by digit on the other device · valid until {time}
messages.settings.security.downgrade.highNote: Needs a co-sign from another device or a recovery code.
messages.settings.security.downgrade.mediumNote: Needs the 6-digit code from this device.
messages.settings.security.rejection.approvalMiss: Approval missing or later than the action
messages.settings.security.rejection.approverNotA: Approving device was not yet admitted
messages.security.dialog.title: Security action
messages.security.code.label: 6-digit code
messages.security.code.help: Open your authenticator app and read the current 6 digits; a code cannot be used twice.
messages.security.upgrade.recoveryOnce.title: Upgrade to High · offline recovery code (shown only once)
messages.security.upgrade.recoveryOnce.intro: “High · device co-sign” is on. The recovery code is the offline key for when the other device is not present.
messages.security.upgrade.title: Upgrade to {level}
messages.security.upgrade.codeIntro: Enter the 6-digit code from this device.
messages.security.upgrade.highBody: Joining, removing and downgrading will then need another admitted device to compare the pairing code; this device generates a one-time recovery code.
messages.security.upgrade.mediumBody: Joining, removing and downgrading will then need this device’s 6-digit code; it stops a casual hand, not a stolen device.
messages.security.downgrade.title: Downgrade to {level}
messages.security.downgrade.coSignIntro: Downgrading from High needs a co-sign from another admitted device (or a recovery code).
messages.security.downgrade.codeIntro: Downgrading from Medium needs the 6-digit code from this device.
messages.security.tier.failed: Could not change the security level: {message}
messages.security.approval.pairingHelp: On another admitted device open “Settings → Security → Security level”, compare the same pairing code and choose “Codes match, approve”.
messages.security.approval.waitingDots: Waiting for another device to approve…
messages.security.approval.whySafe: The pairing code never travels over any channel: both devices derive it from the action digest, so a human comparison is enough.
messages.security.approval.useRecovery: No other device nearby? Use a recovery code
messages.security.approval.recoverySwitchNote: After switching to a recovery code this co-sign request is left to expire; the code is used only to sign locally this time.
messages.security.approval.deniedNote: (visible to the initiating device; this version records no written reason)
messages.security.approval.approvedToast: Approved; the initiating device continues automatically
messages.security.deny.title: Deny this request?
messages.security.totp.import.title: Import authenticator seed
messages.security.totp.import.body: From “Show seed” on another device that holds the seed, paste the grouped text or the otpauth:// URI. The seed never passes through the cloud.
messages.security.totp.import.help: Reconcile the fingerprint with the other device before importing; a mismatch rejects the import.
messages.security.totp.import.missing: Paste the seed text or an otpauth URI.
messages.security.totp.qrUnavailable: QR code unavailable (generation failed): use the grouped text below.
messages.security.totp.seed.title: Authenticator seed
messages.security.totp.seed.warningDefault: The seed is the key to this tier: whoever sees it can pass this tier’s code. Show it in person only between two devices you own.
messages.security.totp.seed.noScreenshot: Do not screenshot or send it in chat; close this after showing it in person.
messages.security.totp.show.title: Show authenticator seed
messages.security.totp.show.intro: Enter this device’s code once before showing the seed (stops a casual glance).
messages.security.totp.generate.title: Generate a shared authenticator seed?
messages.security.totp.generate.body: Only root can generate it. The new seed is written on this device; import it on your other devices so the Medium gate applies consistently.
messages.security.recovery.once.warning: This recovery code appears on screen only once: copy it to offline media (paper, metal or a password tool) and store it apart from the master key backup. Do not screenshot or send it in chat. If lost, it can only be rotated.
messages.security.recovery.once.after: Choose the button below once you have copied it; once this view is gone it cannot be shown again.
messages.security.recovery.rotate.title: Rotate recovery code
messages.security.recovery.rotate.body: Sign with the current recovery code to receive a new one. New signatures with the old code stop working immediately (history already accepted is not reverted).
messages.security.recovery.rotate.help: The new code is shown once; have your offline media ready.
messages.security.recovery.rotate.newIntro: Old keyId {keyId} has been rotated; new signatures with the old code are no longer accepted.
messages.security.recovery.generate.title: Generate a recovery code?
messages.security.recovery.generate.body: A recovery code replaces a co-sign at the High tier when no other device is present. It appears on screen only once; have offline media ready.
messages.security.recovery.error.mismatch: The recovery code does not match the current keyId (it may have been rotated): use the latest code.
messages.security.recovery.error.missing: No recovery code yet: generate or rotate one from the security card first.
messages.security.recovery.error.invalid: Invalid recovery code format: enter all 34 characters (hyphens optional).
messages.security.recovery.error.notApplicable: Not at the High tier: a recovery code only replaces a High co-sign and is not needed here.
messages.security.recovery.error.signFailed: Recovery code signature check failed: retry; if it keeps failing, rotate the code.
messages.security.recovery.code.label: Recovery code
messages.security.recovery.code.help: The 34-character code you stored offline; used only to sign locally, never uploaded or written to browser storage, and the field clears on submit.
messages.security.revoke.viaRecovery.title: Remove device · recovery code
messages.security.revoke.viaRecovery.intro: Currently High · device co-sign. Sign locally with the offline recovery code to write the removal record immediately; the code never passes through the cloud.
messages.security.tier.viaRecovery.title: Downgrade to {level} · recovery code
messages.security.tier.viaRecovery.intro: Currently High · device co-sign. Sign this downgrade with the offline recovery code; the code never passes through the cloud.
messages.security.revoke.title: Remove device
messages.security.revoke.bodyIntro: Policy records signed by {device} will no longer be accepted here and this device stops sending it data; already synced data is not reclaimed; another device can restore it.
messages.security.revoke.gate.high: Currently High · device co-sign: another admitted device must compare the pairing code and approve; this device then completes the removal automatically.
messages.security.revoke.gate.medium: Currently Medium · authenticator code: the next step asks for this device’s 6-digit code.
messages.security.revoke.intro: Policy records signed by {device} will no longer be accepted here; it runs automatically once the co-sign is approved.
messages.security.revoke.codeIntro: Enter this device’s 6-digit code to write the removal record.
messages.security.restore.title: Restore device
messages.security.restore.bodyIntro: {device} will be accepted here again. Restoring starts a new epoch: policy records it signed before the restore (subscriptions, removals and so on) do not come back, and it must declare its subscriptions again.
messages.security.restore.gate.high: Currently High · device co-sign: another admitted device must compare the pairing code and approve; this device then completes the restore automatically.
messages.security.restore.intro: {device} will be restored; policy records from the old epoch do not come back.
messages.security.restore.viaRecovery.title: Restore device · recovery code
messages.security.restore.viaRecovery.intro: Sign locally with the offline recovery code to write the restore record immediately; the code never passes through the cloud.
messages.security.restore.codeIntro: Enter this device’s 6-digit code to write the restore record.
messages.settings.write.restarting: Restarting automatically to apply the configuration…
messages.settings.write.rolledBack: New configuration not in effect: rolled back (see the banner / Advanced · Diagnostics)
messages.settings.restart.confirmBody: This restarts the local daemon (mebular serve) so saved settings waiting for a restart take effect. The console is briefly unavailable and the page reloads when it is back. Continue?
messages.settings.restart.triggered: Restart triggered, waiting for the daemon…
messages.assistants.head.note: Connecting changes one entry in the assistant’s configuration, backed up first; it takes effect after you restart that app.
messages.assistants.empty: No assistants registered yet: choose “+ Add assistant” to start.
messages.assistants.failed.label: Connection failed
messages.assistants.verify.pending: Wired up — takes effect after you restart {name}
messages.assistants.verify.pendingWithNote: Wired up — takes effect after you restart {name} ({note})
messages.assistants.verify.pendingSteps: ① Quit the app completely (end the process, not just the window) ② open it again ③ mebular should appear in its tool list. We never restart it for you.
messages.assistants.verify.failed: Verification failed: fix the failed step above, then choose “Verify again”.
messages.assistants.detail.configOnly: Configuration-level check only (this assistant provides no verification command)
messages.assistants.form.addTitle: Register an AI assistant we do not know yet: give its MCP configuration file, or paste a configuration snippet.
messages.assistants.form.modeFile: Choose a file (merged automatically, backed up first)
messages.assistants.form.modeSnippet: Paste a snippet (snippet only, merge by hand)
messages.assistants.form.name: Name
messages.assistants.form.snippetNote: Snippet mode: this row always shows “Manual needed” and the details offer a copyable snippet — there is never an automatic “Connect”.
messages.assistants.action.verifyReady: Configuration is ready — restart the app to take effect, then choose “I reloaded, verify”.
messages.assistants.action.verifyNotPassed: Verification failed: expand to see the failed step and its output.
messages.assistants.action.copied: Snippet copied; paste it into the assistant’s MCP configuration.
messages.assistants.preview.unchanged: (identical to the current configuration, no change needed)
messages.assistants.rollback.title: Roll back the assistant configuration?
messages.assistants.rollback.body: This restores the assistant’s configuration to its state before connecting (from the automatic backup). Rolling back overwrites the Mebular entry written when connecting.
messages.assistants.done.connectChanged: Connected (original configuration backed up). Takes effect after you restart the assistant.
messages.assistants.form.error.id: The ID must be lowercase kebab-case (for example my-assistant)
messages.assistants.form.error.name: Name is required
messages.assistants.form.error.path: Configuration file path is required (file mode)
messages.assistants.remove.title: Remove the custom assistant?
messages.assistants.remove.body: This removes the registration of “{id}”; its existing configuration file is untouched. Register it again to reconnect later.
messages.settings.security.approval.waitingPrefix: Waiting for another device to approve:
messages.security.totp.seed.fingerprintNote: (reconcile with another device; does not contain the seed itself)
messages.assistants.reloadHintPrefix: Written · takes effect after you restart {name} ·
